purpose: Freeze the common 12S electrical platform and per-ESC hardware capability for the PB-07 1.5-3.0 kW aggregate-propulsion family while keeping Quad/Hexa, payload/MTOW, exact motor/propeller and exact pack implementation open.

change_control.rule: PB-08 inherits PB-07 unless a PB-08 decision explicitly supersedes or closes an OPEN PB-07 field. Any later change to a PB-08 frozen value requires PB-09 or an explicitly linked ECO; no silent overwrite is allowed.

inherited_product_direction.flight_controller_interface: CAN-FD capable with Classic CAN compatibility
inherited_product_direction.arming_policy: power-up/reset DISARMED; independent hardware inhibit final authority; latched fault inhibits PWM; no automatic re-arm

new_frozen_decisions.rationale: The first electrical platform is sized at the top of the user-approved 1.5-3.0 kW family so lower-power variants can be obtained by controlled derating rather than a different base power stage.

Both current propulsion anchors support 12S; system current remains manageable at 3 kW and 12S preserves compatibility with the broad legacy ~48 V hardware class without the extra voltage burden of 14S.
12S x 3.6 V nominal high-rate Li-ion reference convention.
3.0 V/cell loaded design floor. Below this point the system must derate or terminate the mission; exact hard battery cutoff remains pack-specific.
Supports the 3 kW family with either Quad or Hexa and leaves per-channel headroom above normal 750 W Quad / 500 W Hexa screening points.
Provides channel-level maneuver/failure-redistribution headroom without defining the still-open vehicle-level aggregate peak-power policy.
1.0 kW at the 36 V full-power loaded floor is 27.8 A; requirement rounded upward to 30 A.
1.5 kW at 36 V is 41.7 A; 50 A provides additional electrical transient capability margin.
12S full charge is 50.4 V. A 100 V class restores strong compatibility with practical low-RDSon devices and legacy B1 while leaving transient control to a separately frozen terminal-stress target.

The power-stage layout/DC-link/snubber/clamp network shall keep repetitive switch-terminal stress at or below 75 V; normal operation shall not rely on repetitive avalanche. This is a design target, not measured overshoot evidence.
Constant 3 kW for 10 min needs 500 Wh terminal energy; preserving 20% gross reserve requires 625 Wh before auxiliary/conversion/aging margin. 750 Wh prevents sizing at the mathematical edge.

battery_reference_not_selection.note: P50B values are manufacturer-data calculation anchors. Cold/low-SOC/aged sag, pack hardware mass, current sharing, fusing, BMS and thermal qualification remain open.

rotor_architecture_mass_trade.note: Above the break-even per-axis installed mass Quad has greater residual mass budget before extra Hexa arm structure; below it Hexa may retain a mass advantage. Exact frame and custom-axis mass are required before freeze.

remaining_critical_open_items: Quad versus Hexa rotor count and degraded-mode policy
payload/MTOW and complete frame/avionics/mission-equipment mass roll-up
exact production motor/propeller MPN and operating points
phase RMS/peak current and current-sense range
exact 100 V MOSFET MPN/count and gate driver
anti_hallucination_rule: PB-08 freezes design requirements and capability targets only. No manufacturer benchmark or calculation is a custom ESC, battery, vehicle, thermal, dyno or flight validation result.
